topic.title: Networking
topic.description: Addresses, routes, sockets, DNS, HTTP checks and packet capture from a Linux host

commands.name: ip
commands.summary: Show and change addresses, links, routes and neighbors
commands.description: The iproute2 tool for interfaces (link), addresses (addr), routing (route) and ARP/neighbor tables (neigh). Replaces ifconfig, route and arp.

examples.title: Addresses at a glance
examples.scenario: List every interface with its state and IP addresses, one per line.

output_notes.anomaly: DOWN: cable, driver or switch port problem.

examples.title: Default gateway
examples.scenario: Which gateway does this host use for traffic outside its subnets?
examples.output: default via 192.168.1.1 dev eth0 proto dhcp src 192.168.1.15 metric 100

examples.title: Route chosen for a destination
examples.scenario: Which interface and source address will be used to reach 10.20.0.5?

examples.title: ARP table
examples.scenario: Check whether the gateway's MAC address was resolved.

output_notes.anomaly: FAILED or INCOMPLETE: L2 problem or host down.

examples.title: Bring an interface up
examples.scenario: Interface eth1 is DOWN. Bring it up.
examples.command: sudo ip link set eth1 up

use_cases.title: Host unreachable
use_cases.situation: Verify address, link and default route before blaming the network.

pitfalls: Changes made with ip are not persistent; configure netplan or NetworkManager for reboots.

commands.name: ping
commands.summary: Test reachability and latency with ICMP echo
commands.description: Sends ICMP echo requests and reports loss and round-trip time.

examples.title: Five pings
examples.scenario: Check reachability of the gateway 192.168.1.1 with five packets.
examples.output:
5 packets transmitted, 5 received, 0% packet loss, time 4006ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.412/0.530/0.711/0.101 ms

output_notes.anomaly: Any loss on a LAN; > 1% on a WAN.
Large mdev: congestion or wireless issues.

examples.title: Path MTU test
examples.scenario: Check whether 1472-byte packets pass to 10.0.0.1 without fragmentation.
examples.explanation: 1472 bytes payload + 28 bytes of headers = 1500 MTU.

use_cases.title: Is it the network?
use_cases.situation: First check from the affected host to gateway, then to the target.

pitfalls: Many firewalls drop ICMP; no reply does not prove the host is down.

commands.name: traceroute
commands.summary: Show the hops to a destination
commands.description: Sends probes with increasing TTL to reveal each router on the path.

examples.title: Numeric path
examples.scenario: Show the path to 8.8.8.8 without DNS lookups.

examples.title: TCP path through firewalls
examples.scenario: ICMP is filtered. Trace the path to api.example.com using TCP port 443.

use_cases.title: Where does it stop?
use_cases.situation: Find the last responding hop when a remote network is unreachable.

pitfalls: Hops showing * * * may just ignore probes; only a persistent stop is meaningful.

commands.name: ss
commands.description: Lists TCP/UDP sockets, their states, queues and owning processes. Modern replacement for netstat.

flags.description: Owning process (requires root for others' processes).

examples.title: Listening ports with process
examples.scenario: Port 8080 does not answer. List listening TCP and UDP sockets with process, numerically.
examples.output:
Netid State  Recv-Q Send-Q Local Address:Port Process
tcp   LISTEN 0      511    0.0.0.0:80         users:(("nginx",pid=1420,fd=6))

output_notes.meaning: For LISTEN sockets, connections waiting for accept().
output_notes.anomaly: Close to Send-Q (backlog): the app is not accepting fast enough.

examples.title: Connections to a port
examples.scenario: List established TCP connections to local port 443.

examples.title: Socket summary
examples.scenario: Get totals of sockets per state, e.g. to spot TIME-WAIT buildup.

use_cases.title: Service not reachable
use_cases.situation: Confirm the process listens on the expected address and port.

commands.name: dig
commands.description: Sends DNS queries and prints the full answer, including TTLs and the server that answered.

flags.description: Follow delegation from the root servers.

examples.title: Resolve an A record
examples.scenario: Which IP does api.example.com resolve to?

examples.title: Compare resolvers
examples.scenario: Check what the public resolver 1.1.1.1 returns for api.example.com.

examples.title: Mail servers
examples.scenario: List the MX records of example.com.

examples.title: Reverse lookup
examples.scenario: Find the host name of 8.8.8.8.

use_cases.title: DNS change not visible
use_cases.situation: Compare the internal resolver with a public one after a record change.

pitfalls: Caches respect TTLs: an old answer can persist until the TTL expires.

commands.name: curl
commands.summary: Make HTTP requests from the terminal
commands.description: Transfers data over HTTP(S) and many other protocols; ideal for health checks and API debugging.

flags.description: Write the body to a file (/dev/null to discard).

examples.title: Response headers
examples.scenario: Check status and headers returned by https://example.com.

examples.title: Status code only
examples.scenario: Print only the HTTP status code of the local health endpoint.

examples.title: Total request time
examples.scenario: Measure how long the health endpoint takes in total.

examples.title: Full timing breakdown (reference)
examples.scenario: Reference: connect, first byte and total time in one line.
examples.explanation: time_connect: TCP done; time_starttransfer: first byte (server think time); time_total: everything.

examples.title: POST JSON
examples.scenario: POST {"ok":true} as JSON to localhost:8000/api/ping.

use_cases.title: Slow API
use_cases.situation: Separate connection time from server processing time.

commands.name: nc
commands.description: netcat: tests whether a port accepts connections, or sends and receives raw data.

examples.title: Is the port open?
examples.scenario: Check whether db.internal accepts TCP connections on port 5432, waiting 3 seconds at most.

examples.title: Temporary listener
examples.scenario: Open a listener on port 9000 to test a firewall rule from another host.

use_cases.title: Firewall or service?
use_cases.situation: A refused connection means the host answered; a timeout points to filtering.

commands.name: tcpdump
commands.description: Captures packets on an interface with BPF filters; can save to pcap for Wireshark.

flags.description: Write raw packets to a pcap file.

examples.title: Traffic on a port
examples.scenario: Capture 20 packets to or from port 443 on eth0, numerically.

examples.title: Traffic with one host
examples.scenario: Show traffic between this host and 10.0.0.12.

examples.title: Save for Wireshark
examples.scenario: Save DNS traffic on eth0 to dns.pcap for later analysis.

use_cases.title: Is the packet arriving?
use_cases.situation: Prove whether requests reach the host before debugging the app.

pitfalls: Always filter on busy servers; unfiltered captures can drop packets and fill the disk.

commands.name: ssh
commands.description: Connects to remote hosts, runs commands and forwards ports through encrypted tunnels.

examples.title: Custom port and key
examples.scenario: Connect as deploy to app.example.com on port 2222 with key ~/.ssh/deploy.

examples.title: Tunnel to a private database
examples.scenario: Reach PostgreSQL on db.internal:5432 via bastion, exposed locally on 15432.

examples.title: Jump host
examples.scenario: Connect to 10.0.0.20 through the bastion host in one command.

use_cases.title: Private service access
use_cases.situation: Reach an internal database without opening firewall ports.

pitfalls: Permission denied (publickey): check key permissions (600) and run ssh -v.

commands.name: ethtool
commands.summary: NIC speed, duplex and error counters
commands.description: Shows and tunes network interface hardware settings and statistics.

examples.title: Link speed and duplex
examples.scenario: Transfers are slow. Check negotiated speed and duplex of eth0.
examples.output:
Speed: 100Mb/s
Duplex: Half
Link detected: yes

output_notes.meaning: Only one direction at a time.

examples.title: Error counters
examples.scenario: Look for errors or drops in eth0's statistics.

use_cases.title: Slow transfers on one host
use_cases.situation: A bad cable or port often shows as low speed or errors.

procedures.title: Triage a host that cannot reach a remote network
procedures.context: The app server cannot reach the partner API at 203.0.113.10.
procedures.goal: Locate the failing layer: interface, gateway, path or remote port.

steps.interpretation: Timeout: filtered; refused: host up, service closed.

use_cases.title: Partner integration down
use_cases.situation: Prove which side is failing before opening a ticket.

procedures.title: Investigate a DNS answer mismatch
procedures.context: Users reach the old server after api.example.com was moved to a new IP.
procedures.goal: Compare resolvers and find stale caches.

steps.interpretation: The TTL shows how long caches may keep the old address.

procedures.title: Find where an HTTP request spends time
procedures.context: The API feels slow, but only from some hosts.
procedures.goal: Separate network latency from server processing time.

steps.interpretation: Large gap between connect and first byte: the server is slow, not the network.

procedures.title: Verify a new service is reachable
procedures.context: A new service was deployed on port 8080 but clients time out.
procedures.goal: Check the listener locally, then the traffic on the wire.

steps.interpretation: 127.0.0.1:8080 means only local clients can connect.
SYNs without replies: host firewall drops them.

procedures.title: Reach a private database through a bastion
procedures.context: You need psql access to db.internal, reachable only from the bastion host.
procedures.goal: Open a tunnel and test the forwarded port.

steps.purpose: Open the tunnel (-N: no remote shell)
